items.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023
items.q: he calls to say I had the job playing with George Duke and Jean Luc Ponty on the tour in ’73.

ctx.x: Did he write out all those very intricate melodies?

Everything was written out. He had — everything was written out. I got the job with Frank by playing the tuba over the telephone. He was looking for a tuba player for “The Grand Wazoo” and so I played the tuba over the telephone, went over to his house the next day and he says, he says, “Sal Marquez tells me you play other instruments besides the tuba.” And I said, “Yeah.” So he said, “Well give me a list.” And so I put down bass trombone, trombone, trumpet, flugelhorn, piccolo trumpet, tenor sax, flute and…

tour. Then he cut down the band to 6 pieces. And he says, “We’re only going to have one horn on the next tour” and he says, “it’s going to be Bruce Fowler.” I said, “Cool.” He says, “Bruce tells me you play electric bass.” I said, “Yeah.” He says, “Well you want to audition?” I said, “Sure.” I went over to his house one day and I remember Ralph Humphreys was there — he just passed away last week, sadly — and George Duke was there playing keyboards. So I auditioned on electric bass, thought I sounded pretty good.…
